messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT @channel — p99 latency breach detected in runtime cluster us-west-2-runner-3. p95=850ms, p99=2.1s (SLO p99=1.2s). Streaming stalls observed and spike started ~2318005480. Metrics show sharp increase in kv_cache_evictions and prefill_queue_length. Possible KV cache fragmentation / prefill vs decode imbalance. Correlation id examples: cid=86a1.., cid=9b2f..; dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/ops/latency?cluster=us-west-2-runner-3

maria: ack — i'm on call. collecting flamegraphs + eviction timelines. grabbing logs from nodes. :eyes:

aj: i'm watching the prefill queues, notices lots of concurrent prefill requests piling up. looks like prefill workers are CPU-starved, decode workers are mostly idle — weird.

maria: logs show repeated cache eviction due to mem_pressure on the node. sample log:
```
2026-03-15T20:31:12Z runtime[pid=2245]: KVCache: evicting 128 entries, free=120MB, used=980MB, max=1GB
2026-03-15T20:31:13Z runtime[pid=2245]: PrefillWorker: queue_wait_ms=450, decode_latency_ms=30
2026-03-15T20:31:14Z runtime[pid=2245]: Stream: stall detected cid=86a1... stall_ms=1100
```

aj: reproducing locally with load test shows prefill tasks locking the main event loop and causing streaming stalls. prefill > decode by ratio ~4:1.

sre-lead: short-term mitigation options:
- reduce prefill concurrency (config: PREFILL_CONCURRENCY) on affected pool
- increase KV cache size / adjust eviction threshold (KV_MAX_BYTES) for us-west-2-runner-3
- route a fraction of traffic to fallback smaller model without prefill
- temporarily disable prefill for streaming endpoints to avoid stalls

maria: trying quick change — setting PREFILL_CONCURRENCY=2 for pool us-west-2-runner-3. rolling restart on 3 pods.

aj: command I ran:
```
redwoodctl config set runtime.pool.us-west-2-runner-3.PREFILL_CONCURRENCY=2 --env production
kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime-pool-us-west-2-runner-3
```

oncall-2: noted. tagging docs/runbooks/kv-cache-eviction.md as reference. please paste runbook link here.

maria: runbook https://confluence.redwood/ops/kv-cache-eviction-runbook — following step 2 (lower prefill, watch eviction rate).

incident-bot: :information_source: Action taken: PREFILL_CONCURRENCY lowered to 2; rollout started at 2318005558. Automated alert will suppress for 10m.

tim: i'm scaling decoder workers as a test so decode can catch up: `kubectl scale deploy/decoder-workers --replicas=6 -n runtime` — if decode can consume prefill faster, imbalance should reduce.

aj: also pushed KV_MAX_BYTES from 1GB -> 1.25GB on the pool to reduce eviction pressure. command:
```
redwoodctl config set runtime.pool.us-west-2-runner-3.KV_MAX_BYTES=1342177280
```

maria: monitoring p95/p99 and stream stall count. so far after changes (5m): p95 down to 520ms, p99 down to 940ms, stream stalls reduced by ~70%. eviction rate dropped from 320/min -> 40/min.

customer-success: notified Tier-1 customers in us-west about degraded streaming quality between 20:30-20:45 UTC. no data exfiltration or errors reported, only stalls/latency.

sre-lead: good improvement. next steps: continue monitoring, keep PREFILL reduced for 30m, then ramp cautiously while observing eviction rate and stall count. prepare fallback routing plan if it recurs.

oncall-2: taking over on-call now (handoff). summary for next shift: root cause likely KV cache fragmentation combined with prefill flood when certain workload patterns hit long-prefix token sequences; prefill workers were starved/over-scheduled while decode throughput lagged. Mitigations applied: PREFILL_CONCURRENCY=2, KV_MAX_BYTES increased, decoder-workers scaled to 6, 20% traffic routed to smaller model as fallback. Current status: SLOs restored; p99 trending < SLO. Links: dash, runbook, logs.

maria: handing over live charts: https://dash.redwood.internal/ops/latency?range=30m&cluster=us-west-2-runner-3

oncall-2: I'll keep watch for the next 2 hours. if p99 >1.2s again, escalate to runtime-ff.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident created INC-2026-2318005555. Severity: Sev2. Timeline and actions documented to the incident ticket.

tim: leaving note — we should add an autoscale rule: if kv_evictions_rate > 200/min then scale pool + add buffer cache on next infra deploy. filing infra ticket.

customer-success: updating customers that mitigation completed and we're monitoring. thanks for quick responses. :thumbsup:

oncall-2: closing active mitigation. leaving handoff note for follow-up: 1) look into prefill scheduling fairness, 2) analyze hot key patterns that fragment KV, 3) add alert to correlate prefill_queue_length with decode_worker_utilization. assigning to maria/aj for postmortem.

maria: acknowledged — will run postmortem and include replay steps, load test, and config recommendations.

aj: adding logs + sample cids to the incident ticket for trace debugging.

incident-bot: :memo: Post-incident action items created: PIA-2026-78 (investigate prefill scheduling), PIA-2026-79 (cache fragmentation detection), PIA-2026-80 (autoscale + fallback tuning).
